verdict.rationale: uv's own CLI documents scriptable commands for installing and updating dependencies: `uv add` updates pyproject.toml, the lockfile and the environment, and `uv lock --upgrade-package` updates a package. Its documented GitHub Actions integration implies these run in unattended CI. The evidence never documents a non-interactive mode, exit-code semantics or error-reporting format, and one community report describes troubleshooting as diagnostic black boxes. missing for 10: documented exit codes, documented error output/structured failure reporting, explicit non-interactive/no-prompt guarantees, hands-on corroboration of agent-driven use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an agent install and update project dependencies non-interactively, with clear exit codes and errors when something fails

citations.quote: You can add dependencies to your `pyproject.toml` with the `uv add` command. This will also update the lockfile and project environment
The `--upgrade-package` flag will attempt to update the specified package to the latest compatible version, while keeping the rest of the lockfile intact.
we recommend the official `astral-sh/setup-uv` action, which installs uv, adds it to PATH, (optionally) persists the cache, and more
